item.title: Go Daily Question 064
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type A interface {
 ShowA() int
}

type B interface {
 ShowB() int
}

type Work struct {
 i int
}

func (w Work) ShowA() int {
 return w.i + 10
}

func (w Work) ShowB() int {
 return w.i + 20
}

func main() {
 c := Work{3}
 var a A = c
 var b B = c
 fmt.Println(a.ShowA())
 fmt.Println(b.ShowB())
}

item.title: Go Daily Question 056
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type People struct{}

func (p *People) ShowA() {
 fmt.Println("showA")
 p.ShowB()
}
func (p *People) ShowB() {
 fmt.Println("showB")
}

type Teacher struct {
 People
}

func (t *Teacher) ShowB() {
 fmt.Println("teacher showB")
}

func main() {
 t := Teacher{}
 t.ShowA()
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: “showA” “showB”

t.ShowA() will prioritize calling its own ShowA(). However, since it’s not defined in the problem, it calls the parent struct’s ShowA(). When it reaches p.ShowB(), note that p is *People, the parent struct, and it will call p’s own ShowB(). Therefore, the output is: “showA” “showB”

item.title: Go Daily Question 052
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type People struct{}

func (p *People) ShowA() {
 fmt.Println("showA")
 p.ShowB()
}
func (p *People) ShowB() {
 fmt.Println("showB")
}

type Teacher struct {
 People
}

func (t *Teacher) ShowB() {
 fmt.Println("teacher showB")
}

func main() {
 t := Teacher{}
 t.ShowB()
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: teacher showB t.ShowB() will use its own existing ShowB(). If you want to use the parent struct’s (People) ShowB(), you need to change it to t.People.ShowB().

item.title: Go Daily Question 045
item.description:
Will the following code compile?

package main

import (
 "fmt"
)

type worker interface {
 work()
}

type person struct {
 name string
 worker
}

func main() {
 var w worker = person{}
 fmt.Println(w)
}

A: Yes; B: No; C: Don’t know

🔑 Answer Analysis:

A

Interfaces can be embedded in Go structs.

Embedded interfaces have practical uses. Example: In the standard library sort package, there is an interface: Interface

type Interface interface {
 // Len is the number of elements in the collection.
 Len() int
 // Less reports whether the element with
 // index i should sort before the element with index j.
 Less(i, j int) bool
 // Swap swaps the elements with indexes i and j.
 Swap(i, j int)
}
type reverse struct {
 // This embedded Interface permits Reverse to use the methods of
 // another Interface implementation.
 Interface
}

It embeds an Interface to reverse sorting.
